# `trigger_test_crash`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Deliberately crash the control process (crash-reporter test hook).

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xa8270, signal handler @0xa7640, main @0x9c260, CrashHandler::Start @0x7074c0 (64-bit build); handler @0x4c830 (32-bit build) |

Takes no parameters. The handler logs an intentional-crash message and raises signal 11 (SIGSEGV); it adds no result, code or error. No successful reply is established, and the connection is expected to drop. The signal number is not a JSON-RPC code. On the fault the control process logs the signal, finalises any AVI recording, writes a crash dump through an external crash reporter and terminates with the default signal action (READ handler; INFERRED order). The process does not restart itself; whether the host restarts it is unresolved. DESTRUCTIVE: terminates the control process and interrupts any running session. No app emitter was found.

Side effects: Terminates the control process via SIGSEGV after logging, AVI finalisation and a crash dump. No state guard. Restart by the host and network teardown behaviour are unresolved.

{"id":81,"method":"trigger_test_crash"}
